purpose: M2 database credential lookup foundation; no HTTP authentication, token issuer, upload service, deployment or performance claim.

beforeAfter.before: The harness applies storage migration 001 and asserts that neither api_credentials nor resolve_api_credential(bytea) exists. This is missing functionality, not an old deployed authorization vulnerability.
beforeAfter.after: Migration 002 resolves an active synthetic editor key to its stored tenant/project and read,ingest scopes; a membership downgrade returns read, revocation returns zero rows, membership removal/rejoin does not resurrect the key.

checks.result: 31 passed, zero failed/skipped; real PostgreSQL 17.11 (Debian 17.11-1.pgdg13+2), pinned image, no network/external DB, owned container removed. Includes actual separately connected restricted lookup login.

manualReview.scope: SQL role/grant separation, forced row policies, fixed definer search path, finite statement-time expiry, current-role intersection, membership removal, digest bounds, reapply rollback, and docs claims. No independent specialized security review is claimed.

limitations: Stored SHA-256 digests must come from high-entropy random API secrets, not passwords. Generation, format, hashing/parsing and issuance are next slices.
HTTP routes must require returned identity and operation scope and use only its stored tenant/project; no route is implemented here.
Authorization uses statement snapshots; revocation does not cancel already-authorized requests.
Membership applies to all tenant projects; no per-project member assignments exist.
Migration owner is trusted and remains separate from runtime logins. Never grant auth_owner to a runtime login.
No public schema/root package export or runtime dependency changed. Portable operation remains database-free; M2 is open.

initialHeadCi.review: CodeRabbit completed review with three findings. They are addressed in the follow-up, not ignored because CI passed.

findings.issue: Documented non-superuser CREATEROLE migration owner cannot transfer function ownership without SET permission.
findings.beforeResult: One failure, SQLSTATE 42501: must be able to SET ROLE eval_hosted_auth_owner. Isolated container removed.
findings.resolution: Grant the trusted migration owner SET with inheritance disabled; grant runtime function execution while still owning the function, before transferring ownership. Apply both migrations as a real non-superuser database owner in the harness.

findings.issue: 300ms active expiry window can fail if CI pauses before the first lookup.
findings.resolution: Use an already-elapsed expiry anchored one microsecond after transaction start, then verify it is after transaction time but before current statement time. There is no first-active-lookup deadline. Other tests cover active keys.
findings.counterexampleInput: Deliberately replace statement_timestamp() with now() in the local migration only, run the focused check, and restore exact correct bytes in finally. This control is not old deployed behavior.
findings.counterexampleResult: Expected failure: wrong transaction clock returns 1 active identity; correct statement clock returns 0.

findings.issue: Record actual raw CI evidence before closing status update.
findings.resolution: Inspect initial-head raw jobs above, link STATUS to this revision-specific record and PR #110. Final follow-up head is verified and replied on the PR before merge, without relabeling initial-head results as later-head results.
